page: Vultr vcg-a16-2c-8g-2vram is an entry-level instance in the Cloud GPU family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel x86_64 core with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a 16 MB L3 cache and supports AVX and AES instructions. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and includes one public IPv4 address.

The instance is equipped with a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU, representing a 0.125 slice of the physical card and providing 2 GB of dedicated VRAM. Benchmark data indicates average single-core CPU performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1428.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1781.78. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the weak category, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2612.0 and uncached memory write speeds of 19.81 GB/sec. Ray tracing performance is poor, reflecting the limited fractional GPU allocation.

Despite the weak multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, the hardware excels in lightweight LLM inference. It achieves a top-tier prompt processing speed of 7078.28 tokens/sec for a small 135M parameter model, alongside an average text generation speed of 233.47 tokens/sec. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing reaches an average speed of 117.16 tokens/sec. This profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for developers requiring entry-level GPU acceleration for small-scale model inference, lightweight graphics rendering, or testing GPU-enabled applications without the expense of a full dedicated GPU.
